children: Diesel prices surged above $6 a gallon for the first time on record, raising concerns about renewed energy-driven inflation just ahead of the fuel’s peak-demand season.
The national average reached $6.0556 a gallon, according to the American Automobile Association. In California, prices were approaching $8 a gallon.
Fuel costs are climbing as crude oil prices surge following a sharp escalation in fighting between the U.S. and Iran this month. U.S. crude futures
topped $100 a barrel on Thursday for the first time since May and are up roughly 20% in September.

The surge in fuel costs is particularly challenging for President Donald Trump’s Republican Party, with just over 50 days remaining before the midterm elections. Higher prices could be especially consequential in Maine, where heating oil is used by a larger share of households than anywhere else in the country, as well as in agricultural states such as Ohio, Kansas, and Iowa.
However, the White House has limited options to bring domestic fuel prices down. Beyond another release from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, an export ban is one of the few remaining levers.

U.S. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said “every idea is on the table” when asked about potential diesel export controls, while acknowledging that similar measures have pushed prices higher in the past.
